transcript.text: Hi, we've just had a Bosch KGN36VLEAG delivered last week and it makes a gurgling, bubbling sound like water running, plus a click every so often and a crack noise at night. Is it faulty? It's driving my husband mad.

Those sounds are usually normal for a modern frost-free fridge-freezer, especially during the first week or two:

• Gurgling / bubbling / water-running sound: normally refrigerant moving through the cooling pipes, or water draining during the automatic defrost cycle.
• Occasional click: often the compressor switching on or off, or a control/defrost component operating.
• Crack / creak, particularly overnight: plastic liners and pipes expand and contract as temperatures change; frost/ice can also make a cracking sound during defrosting. Night-time makes it seem much louder because the room is quiet.

It is less likely to be a fault if it is cooling and freezing properly, the sounds are intermittent, and there is no water leak or error indication.

A few practical things can reduce perceived noise:

1. Check it is level and stable — it should not rock when pressed at the corners. Adjust the front feet if needed.
2. Make sure it is not touching a wall, cabinet or pipework, as vibration can be amplified. Use the clearance specified in its Bosch installation instructions.
3. Ensure bottles, shelves and items inside are not rattling against each other.
4. Avoid pushing it tightly into an enclosed unit; adequate ventilation is important.
5. If it was moved after delivery, it should have been left upright for several hours before being switched on. At this point that is unlikely to be relevant, but it can make early operation noisier.

Contact Bosch/the retailer under the warranty if any of the following apply:

• it makes a repeated clicking every few minutes but does not cool;
• the compressor is constantly very loud or struggles to start;
• there is a burning smell, excessive heat, tripped electrics, or a leak;
• the noise is a harsh grinding, metallic banging, or very loud vibration rather than occasional gurgles/clicks/cracks;
• temperatures are not holding roughly 3–5°C in the fridge and –18°C in the freezer after it has had a day or so to settle.

If you can, record 30–60 seconds of the sound and note how often it happens. Bosch support can usually tell from a recording whether it is normal operation. Based on the noises you describe alone, though, it sounds typical rather than faulty.
